question: 17th Parallel was the boundary between which two countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**North Vietnam and South Vietnam**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 17th Parallel served as the boundary between North Vietnam and South Vietnam following the Geneva Accords of 1954.
 
• The division was intended to be temporary, with plans for reunification elections that never occurred due to political tensions.
 
• The 17th Parallel became a significant military line during the Vietnam War, marking the border where opposing forces operated.
 
• The boundary led to the separation of families and communities, contributing to social and economic challenges in both regions during and after the conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Germany and France**

 
• Germany and France have a long history of rivalry, particularly during the 19th and 20th centuries, including conflicts such as the** Franco-Prussian War and World War I and II.**
 
• Both are founding members of the **European Union**, promoting integration.
 
• Germany has the largest economy in Europe, with France being a significant economic player.
 
• They work closely on security, climate change, and defense through the Franco-German Council of Ministers.

**Brazil and Chile**

 
• The border between Brazil and Chile is primarily defined by the **Andes Mountains,** which serve as a natural barrier.
 
• The boundary is approximately **3,500 kilometers** (2,175 miles) long, running from the southern tip of South America to the northern regions.
 
• The border was established through treaties, including the **Treaty of Peace and Friendship in 1884**, resolving territorial disputes between the two countries.

**USA and Canada**

 
• The border between the USA and Canada is the **longest international land border in the world,** stretching approximately **8,891 kilometers** (5,525 miles).
 
• The boundary was established through various treaties, including the **Treaty of Paris (1783) and the Oregon Treaty (1846)**, which resolved territorial disputes.
 
• The border is largely demilitarized, with a focus on peaceful coexistence, allowing for open trade and travel between the two countries.
